findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.comment: Inspectors observed the handwashing sink at the bar to be out of paper towels. PIC was made aware and restocked the paper towels at this handwashing sink to correct the violation. Ensure that all handwashing sinks are stocked with a hand drying device or disposable towels at all times of food preparation and operation.
findings.citation_text: 6-301.12 Hand Drying Provision. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; or (C) A heated-air hand drying device; or (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures.

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment: Inspectors observed raw chicken to be stored above other raw animal proteins in the outdoor walk in cooler. PIC was made aware and instructed staff members to relocate the raw chicken to be stored below other raw animal proteins. Ensure that all food is stored where it is protected from cross contamination.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Inspectors observed the frozen drink dispenser nozzles to have visible soil accumulation. PIC was made aware that this portion of the dispensers need to be cleaned frequently. Ensure that food contact surfaces are cleaned frequently to avoid soil accumulation.
findings.citation_text: 4-602.11(E) Equipment Food-Contact Surfaces and Utensils. (E) Except when dry cleaning methods are used as specified under § 4-603.11, surfaces of UTENSILS and EQUIPMENT contacting FOOD that is not TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be cleaned: (1) At any time when contamination may have occurred; (2) At least every 24 hours for iced tea dispensers and CONSUMER self service UTENSILS such as tongs, scoops, or ladles; (3) Before restocking CONSUMER self-service EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS such as condiment dispensers and display containers; and (4) In EQUIPMENT such as ice bins and BEVERAGE dispensing nozzles and enclosed components of EQUIPMENT such as ice makers, cooking oil storage tanks and distribution lines, BEVERAGE and syrup dispensing lines or tubes, coffee bean grinders, and water vending EQUIPMENT: (a) At a frequency specified by the manufacturer, or (b) Absent manufacturer specifications, at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil or mold.

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored.
findings.comment: Inspectors observed a knife stored in the crevice between two prep coolers. PIC was made aware and the knife was removed and sent to the dish machine to be washed to correct the violation. Inspectors suggested magnetic knife rack or other storage area for knives. Ensure that utensils are stored in a frequently cleaned and sanitized space.
findings.citation_text: 3-304.12(C) In-Use Utensils, Between-Use Storage. During pauses in FOOD preparation or dispensing, FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored:(C) On a clean portion of the food preparation table or cooking equipment only if the in-use utensil and the food-contact surface of the food preparation table or cooking equipment are cleaned and sanitized at a frequency specified under §§ 4-602.11 and 4-702.11.

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting.
findings.comment: There weren’t any signed employee health forms for any of the employees working at the facility. The owner had two blank copies of employee reporting forms and an additional blank copy was given to the facility. Each employee shall have the employee health form signed to acknowledge that they wont come into work sick and that they will report to the PIC if any illnesses are present. Will follow-up on 4/24/2026 to ensure that forms have been signed and completed by all employees.
findings.citation_text: 2-103.11(P) Person In Charge. The PERSON IN CHARGE shall ensure that: (P) FOOD EMPLOYEES and CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEES are informed in a verifiable manner of their responsibility to report in accordance with LAW, to the PERSON IN CHARGE, information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through FOOD, as specified under 2-201.11(A).

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment: Observed an employee use bare hands to operate faucet handles after completing the handwashing process. The activity was ceased and corrected on site. Discussed always using a barrier to turn off faucet handles when completing the handwashing process. The employee rewashed his hands in the correct manner. Ensure to use a barrier when operating faucet handles to prevent recontaminating freshly washed hands.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.12(C) Cleaning Procedure. (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.comment:
IBoth hand-sinks were observed obstructed in the following areas:
- bar hand-sink was blocked with a cutting board and a food cutter
- hand-sink along dish washing line contained scrubbers inside of the basin

The items were removed from both sinks to correct the violation. Discussed with owner. Be sure to educate employees on the importance of handwashing and to avoid obstructing handsinks so that they are easily accessible at all times to wash hands.
findings.citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: The baffles of the ice machine in the back of the house was observed with black debris on the surfaces. Shown to the PIC and he mentioned that he would contact a technician to have the machine cleaned internally. Ensure that food contact surfaces are cleaned as often as necessary to prevent debris accumulation.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
findings.comment: Observed at least two different time/temperature control for safety (TCS) foods stored at room temperature. The owner mentioned that the items were recently cooked and were suppose to be in the process of cooling. The items were tomato sauce and shelled eggs. The owner mentioned that the eggs are served with ramen dishes, which the shell is typically removed from the egg, causing it to be TCS. The items were properly placed on ice baths to correct the violation. When cooling TCS foods, ensure that items are cooled within the six hour timeframe using the approved methods of ice baths, ice wands, adding ice as a component, or inside of cold holding equipment.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.15(A) Cooling Methods. (A) Cooling shall be accomplished in accordance with the time and temperature criteria specified under § 3-501.14 by using one or more of the following methods based on the type of FOOD being cooled: (1) Placing the food in shallow pans; (2) Separating the food into smaller or thinner portions; (3) Using rapid cooling equipment; (4) Stirring the food in a container placed in an ice water bath; (5) Using containers that facilitate heat transfer; (6) Adding ice as an ingredient; or (7) Other effective methods.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
findings.comment: There were not any sanitizer buckets available, although food service was occuring. Discussed with the PIC and sanitizer buckets were prepared and tested at 200ppm (quat). Buckets were placed in various stations of the restaurant to correct the violation. Be sure to educate employees that sanitizer solutions must always be available if preparing, handling, or serving food. Ensure that sanitizer solutions are available during all hours of operation.
findings.citation_text: 4-303.11(B) Cleaning Agents and Sanitizers, Availability. (B) Except for those that are generated on-site at the time of use, chemical SANITIZERS that are used to sanitize EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-7, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
findings.comment: The facility typically uses quaternary ammonium as the chemical for sanitizing food contact surfaces, however, quat test strips were not available. Discussed with the owner that quat test strips will have to be purchased for accurately testing sanitizer solutions. Be sure that test strips are available to ensure that solutions are testing at the manufacturer’s recommended concentration levels. Will follow-up on 4/24/2026.
findings.citation_text: 4-302.14 Sanitizing Solutions, Testing Devices. A test kit or other device that accurately measures the concentration in MG/L of SANITIZING solutions shall be provided.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: There was a ceiling tile that was removed inside of the kitchen area (near the hand-sink along the cook-line). Shown to the owner and he mentioned placing the tile back into place. Additionally, the fan grates (also near the hand-sink along the cook-line) were heavily accumulated with dust. Ensure that physical facilities are maintained in good repair.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Food handler training
findings.comment:
Food handler certificates were not available for any of the employees working at the time of the inspection. Discussed with PIC that any employee that handles food, clean dishes, or ice must obtain a food handler certificate. Ensure that food handler certificates are printed and available for all employees who are not food manager certified.  

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Inspector observed there to be no sanitizer buckets available in the kitchen. Discussed with PIC, and PIC made sanitizer buckets immediately. Ensure that there is always sanitizer solution available to staff when food is being handled.
findings.citation_text: 4-702.11 Before Use After Cleaning. UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be SANITIZED before use after cleaning.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.comment: Inspector observed some TCS foods in a prep table to not be at proper cold-holding temperatures. Items were: two trays of cotija cheese (51F), a tray of diced tomato (47F), cups of salsa verde (66F), mayonnaise (49F), chicken broth (47F), various sauces (60F, 60F, 60F,61F, 66F, 54F), Parmesan cheese (55F), Eggs (52F), vinaigrette (60F), and mashed potatoes (47F). All foods were discarded voluntarily. Ensure that food is always stored at 41F or below. Discarding the food makes this violation corrected on site. Inspector will still return for violation 33.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment: Inspector observed there to be several foods without date marks in various kitchen coolers. Discussed with PIC, and pic could confirm that all items were made within the last seven days. Ensure that all TCS items are marked with a date mark within 24 hours of opening or production of food. Never keep this food longer than 7 days after date marking. Inspector will return 12/22 to re-inspect date marking practices.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.18(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Disposition. (A) A FOOD specified in 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in 3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or PACKAGE that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in 3-501.17(A).

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored and used.
findings.comment: Inspector observed two bleach spray bottles without a label on them. Upon discussion, PIC had the bottles labeled with the common name of the cleaner. Ensure that all toxic chemicals in the kitchen are labeled.
findings.citation_text: 7-102.11 Common Name. Working containers used for storing POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS such as cleaners and SANITIZERS taken from bulk supplies shall be clearly and individually identified with the common name of the material.

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
findings.comment: Inspector observed the large lidless prep cooler on the kitchen line to be failing to hold temperature. For temperatures, see violation 22. Ensure that all cold-holding units being used to store food are capable of holding food at 41F or below. Inspector will return 12/22 to re-inspect the cooler.
findings.citation_text: 4-301.11 Cooling, Heating, and Holding Capacities. EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3.

findings.title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM
findings.comment:
The Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM) on-duty today did not have an allergen certification. Ensure that all CFPMs have valid allergen certifications.

410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Training programs must be accredited by the American National Standards Institute or another reputable accreditation agency under the ASTM International E2659-09 (Standard Practice for Certificate Programs). There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training.
